title: Slide to Complete component for React & Next.js
description: Slide to Complete interaction component for React and Next.js: drag a handle from start to end of a track to confirm actions like payments, approvals, and unlocks.

intro: The Slide to Complete component requires users to drag a handle from the start position to the end of a track before the action is considered complete. It supports configurable thresholds, disabled/loading states, and keyboard completion.

faqs.question: Does the Slide to Complete work with keyboard navigation?
faqs.answer: Yes. The thumb can be focused via Tab key and completed using Space or Enter. Arrow keys can also adjust progress.

faqs.question: Can I customize the appearance of the slider?
faqs.answer: Yes. The component ships 17+ appearance tokens (default, primary, secondary, success, destructive, warning, info, several accent colors, gradients, and a glass variant) plus sm/md/lg size variants, all overridable through CSS variables.

faqs.question: What happens if the user releases before reaching the threshold?
faqs.answer: By default, the thumb snaps back to the start position. This behavior can be changed with the resetOnRelease prop.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The component uses a drag interaction model where the user slides a thumb along a track. Progress is normalized between 0 and 1. When the threshold (default 0.9) is crossed, the component triggers the onComplete callback and animates the thumb to the end position.

sections.heading: Compound API
sections.body: Users can compose the component from primitives: <SlideToComplete.Root>, <SlideToComplete.Track>, <SlideToComplete.Progress>, <SlideToComplete.Label>, <SlideToComplete.Thumb>, and <SlideToComplete.Icon>. The root owns all interaction state and context, while children consume it.

sections.heading: Keyboard interaction
sections.body: Tab to focus the thumb, then use Space or Enter to complete the action. Arrow keys (←/→) can adjust progress. The component supports disabled and loading states that prevent keyboard completion.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.body: The thumb is a semantic button element. Accessible label comes from the label prop or aria-label. Keyboard focus is managed, and reduced motion preferences are respected. Test with screen readers for your specific use case.

sections.heading: State variants
sections.body: The component supports idle, dragging, completing, completed, resetting, and disabled states. Visual styling can be customized via data attributes (data-state, data-appearance, data-size) and CSS variables.
